payload.summary: Multiple active heads for one kind/subject are reported by validate but do not block reads, cache preparation, init or adds to other groups; validate --allow-divergent-heads reports them as warnings instead of errors.
rationale: Canonical records live in Git, so parallel branches superseding or starting the same subject merge cleanly into divergent heads.
Blocking every operation on one conflicted subject disabled Encephalon for all agents until a manual resolver landed.
Strict validate in CI broke main whenever parallel agent pull requests touched one subject, so repositories need an opt-in that keeps every other check strict.
rules: Reads accept a corpus whose only validation issues are MULTIPLE_ACTIVE_HEADS and expose every conflicting head as active.
Writes block MULTIPLE_ACTIVE_HEADS only for kind/subject groups that contain a candidate record, so a resolver must supersede every head of its group.
Blocking decisions use the untruncated issue list; VALIDATION_FAILED details include recordId where an issue has one.
allowDivergentHeads moves only MULTIPLE_ACTIVE_HEADS into warnings; warnings is present only when the option is true, so default validate output stays byte-identical.
CLI --help must stay identical to the published release (release-compatibility check), so new flags are documented in the contract and README, not help.

subject: canonical.active-head-conflicts
